enonce.texte:
Associez chaque émotion à sa définition en anglais. Reliez le mot de la colonne de gauche à sa définition de droite.

Colonne A (Émotions) : happy, sad, angry, tired, worried, scared, excited, bored

Colonne B (Définitions) :
1. When you feel fear because something is dangerous.
2. When you are not interested in what is happening.
3. When you are very pleased about something.
4. When you are very enthusiastic and looking forward to something.
5. When you feel that something bad might happen.
6. When you are not happy and feel low.
7. When you feel strong displeasure or frustration.
8. When you need rest or sleep.

questions.texte: Identifiez et associez chaque émotion à sa définition correcte.
questions.reponse: happy-3, sad-6, angry-7, tired-8, worried-5, scared-1, excited-4, bored-2

sousQuestions.texte: Quelle émotion décrit une personne qui a besoin de repos ?

enonce.texte: Complétez les phrases suivantes avec l'adjectif d'émotion approprié : happy, sad, angry, tired, worried, scared, excited, bored, proud, surprised

questions.texte: Choisissez l'adjectif d'émotion qui convient pour compléter chaque phrase.

enonce.texte:
Lisez les situations suivantes et identifiez l'émotion que chaque personne ressent probablement. Utilisez le vocabulaire approprié.

Situations :
1. A student just received a perfect score on a difficult test.
2. A woman missed her bus and will be late for an important meeting.
3. A child lost his favorite toy.
4. A man is walking alone at night in an unfamiliar neighborhood.
5. A teenager is waiting to see his favorite singer in concert.
6. A woman has been studying for 6 hours without a break.

questions.texte: Identifiez l'émotion ressentie dans chaque situation.

sousQuestions.texte: What emotion does the student feel?
What emotion does the woman feel after missing her bus?
What emotion does the child feel?
What emotion does the man feel in the unfamiliar neighborhood?
What emotion does the teenager feel?
What emotion does the student feel after studying for 6 hours?

enonce.texte:
Répondez aux questions suivantes en utilisant des adjectifs d'émotion et des phrases complètes.

Vocabulaire utile : happy, sad, angry, tired, worried, scared, excited, bored, proud, surprised, nervous, calm, relaxed, stressed, confused, disappointed

questions.texte: Décrivez comment vous vous sentez dans chaque situation.

sousQuestions.texte: How do you feel when you receive a gift?
How do you feel when you wake up early in the morning?
How do you feel when you have an exam?
How do you feel when you are with your friends?

enonce.texte: Dans la vie quotidienne, nous devons souvent réagir aux émotions des autres. Lisez chaque situation et écrivez une réponse appropriée pour montrer de l'empathie.

questions.texte: Rédigez une réponse pour montrer de l'empathie dans chaque situation.

sousQuestions.texte: Your friend says: 'I lost my job today.' How do you react?
sousQuestions.reponse: I'm so sorry to hear that. Are you okay? I'm here for you.

sousQuestions.texte: Your friend says: 'I received a promotion at work!' How do you react?
sousQuestions.reponse: That's great! Congratulations! I'm so happy for you!

sousQuestions.texte: Your friend says: 'I'm really worried about my exams.' How do you react?
sousQuestions.reponse: Don't worry too much. You studied hard, I'm sure you will do well.

sousQuestions.texte: Your friend says: 'My grandmother passed away yesterday.' How do you react?
sousQuestions.reponse: I'm so sorry to hear that. My condolences. I'm here if you need to talk.

intitule: What Makes You Feel This Way?

enonce.texte: Nous ressentons différentes émotions pour différentes raisons. Pour chaque émotion, donnez une situation qui la provoque.

questions.texte: Pour chaque émotion, décrivez une situation qui la provoque chez vous.

sousQuestions.texte: What makes you feel happy? Give a specific example.
sousQuestions.reponse: I feel happy when I spend time with my family and friends.

sousQuestions.texte: What makes you feel sad? Give a specific example.
sousQuestions.reponse: I feel sad when I see people suffering or when I miss someone.

sousQuestions.texte: What makes you feel angry? Give a specific example.
sousQuestions.reponse: I feel angry when people are unfair or disrespectful.

sousQuestions.texte: What makes you feel worried? Give a specific example.
sousQuestions.reponse: I feel worried when I have important exams or when a family member is sick.

sousQuestions.texte: What makes you feel excited? Give a specific example.
sousQuestions.reponse: I feel excited when I'm going on vacation or when I'm about to see someone I love.

enonce.texte: Complétez les phrases avec l'adjectif ou l'adverbe approprié. Utilisez les mots suivants : happy, happily, sad, sadly, angry, angrily, tired, worried, excited

questions.texte: Choisissez entre l'adjectif et l'adverbe pour compléter chaque phrase.

sousQuestions.texte: She smiled ______ when she saw her friend. (happy / happily)
He looked ______ because he lost his wallet. (sad / sadly)
She spoke ______ to her brother. (angry / angrily)
He feels ______ about his trip to London. (excited / excitedly)
She is ______ because she didn't sleep well. (tired / tiredly)

enonce.texte: Imaginez que vous êtes dans chaque situation. Écrivez ce que vous diriez pour exprimer de l'empathie et réagir aux émotions de la personne.

questions.texte: Rédigez une réponse empathique pour chaque situation.

sousQuestions.texte: Your colleague is stressed because of work. What do you say?
sousQuestions.reponse: I understand how you feel. This project is difficult. Would you like some help with it?

sousQuestions.texte: Your friend is sad because she failed her driving test. What do you say?
sousQuestions.reponse: I'm sorry to hear that. Don't worry, you can try again. I'm sure you will succeed next time.

sousQuestions.texte: Your brother is angry because he broke his phone. What do you say?
sousQuestions.reponse: I understand you're upset. It's frustrating when things break. Maybe we can find a solution together.

sousQuestions.texte: Your friend is excited about her new job. What do you say?
sousQuestions.reponse: That's wonderful! I'm so happy for you. You deserve this opportunity.

enonce.texte: Écrivez un petit texte (5-6 phrases) pour décrire comment vous vous sentez aujourd'hui. Utilisez au moins 4 adjectifs d'émotion et justifiez vos sentiments.

questions.texte: Rédigez un paragraphe sur vos émotions du jour.
questions.reponse:
Exemple de réponse :
Today, I feel very happy and relaxed because I spent time with my family. I'm also a little worried about my exams next week, but I'm not scared because I studied a lot. In the morning, I was tired because I woke up early, but now I feel more energetic. I feel proud of what I accomplished today. Overall, it's a good day!

sousQuestions.texte: Comment vous sentez-vous aujourd'hui et pourquoi ? (Utilisez au moins 4 adjectifs)

enonce.texte: Vous avez une conversation avec un ami qui traverse une période difficile. Utilisez le vocabulaire des émotions et des expressions d'empathie pour lui montrer votre soutien.

questions.texte: Rédigez un dialogue complet entre vous et votre ami.
questions.reponse:
Exemple de dialogue :
You: Hey, how are you today? You look sad.
Friend: Yes, I'm a little sad. I had a difficult week at work.
You: I'm sorry to hear that. What happened?
Friend: I received a lot of criticism from my boss. It made me feel worried and stressed.
You: I understand how you feel. That must be very difficult. But you are a good employee, don't be too hard on yourself.
Friend: Thank you for saying that. I feel a little better now.
You: Would you like to talk about it? I'm here to listen.
Friend: Yes, that would help. Thank you for being there for me.
You: Of course. That's what friends are for!

sousQuestions.texte: Quelle émotion votre ami ressent-il ?
sousQuestions.reponse: Il se sent triste, inquiet et stressé.

sousQuestions.texte: Comment avez-vous réagi pour montrer votre soutien ?
sousQuestions.reponse: J'ai montré de l'empathie en écoutant, en comprenant ses sentiments, et en lui offrant mon soutien.
